Commentary.Commentary: That's it from this game! We will be back on 27th March, Sunday and it's a double-header. First, England Women will take on Bangladesh Women at 3.30 am IST (10 pm GMT, previous day). A win for England would mean they would qualify for the semis. Later, it's going to be India Women vs South Africa Women at 6.30 am IST (1 am GMT). India need a win here to qualify for the semis otherwise West Indies Women would go through. All this spices up things nicely for the final day of the league fixtures before we head to the knockouts. Do join us for both the games but the buildup will begin much in advance. Don't forget to join us for that. Until then, it's cheers!

Sophie Divine, the victorious skipper, says she is gutted she did not go ahead in the tournament but wishes well for the teams who have done so. Adds she is thankful for the support. Mentions it is time for her to step away now and reflect on what has happened, refresh and then come back. Adds she still has the hunger to play more but she needs to take some time out and then see what happens. Ends by saying they have been dreaming about the World Cup and they might not play another World Cup at home and it is a big moment for them.

Bismah Maroof, the Pakistan skipper, is in for a chat. She says they could not grab the opportunities in the field and leaked a few extra runs. Adds if she and Dar could’ve continued to play on, things could’ve been different for them. Mentions, even after coming close in a lot of games, they certainly have ticked a lot of boxes over the course of the tournament and would look to come back stronger the next time around.

Suzie Bates is adjudged as the Player of the Match for her exceptional effort with the blade. She says they got rid of their emotions when they lost against England, they have had great support and they enjoyed playing the tournament. Adds they just wanted to enjoy the game. Mentions it just has not gone their way in this tournament, she just wanted to score runs like always. Credits Rowe for the way she bowled and wanted her to get the Player of the Match Award. Rowe now joins in and she says she is pleased with her performance and it is her first five-wicket haul. Mentions it has been a tough week for them but they have had a lot of time to get over it and put in a good performance here.
Stay tuned for the presentation...

New Zealand had runs on the board and they made sure that Pakistan were always behind the asking rate. The bowlers did well to contain runs and never allowed the batters to settle. There was a partnership brewing between Dar and Maroof but Hannah Rowe was surely the game-changer for the White Ferns. Her first spell recorded 3-0-27-0 but she produced a magical second spell. She grabbed 5 wickets and turned the game around completely. The others complimented her well and the hosts have got a thumping win here in front of their home fans in their final league match.

A massive collapse sees Pakistan on the losing side! Pakistan came out with the right intent to chase down the target of 266. The opening stand of Sidra Ameen and Muneeba Ali made sure to built a solid foundation at the top. But they lost both the openers in quick succession. Omaima Sohail did get off to a decent start but slipped out eventually. Later, it was the stand between Maroof and Dar which brought justice to the foundation built by the openers. The pair stitched a stand of 82 runs before Maroof holed out. It went downhill for Pakistan since the loss of their skipper. But the last-wicket stand of Pakistan made sure to bat till the final delivery.

Oh, my word! What a game this has been. Both the teams fought hard but, in the end, White Ferns managed to end their tournament on a high. They won the game by 71 runs, which still gives them an outside chance to make it to the semis. Although it looks very unlikely. Pakistan did put a great fight but unfortunately, they end their tournament with a loss. This campaign has not been fruitful for this Asian side, but they will take a lot of learning back home.

OUT! CAUGHT! A brilliant take here by Sophie Devine. Muneeba Ali's entertaining innings comes to an end. Rosemary Mair strikes in her second over. It is fuller, straight and on off. Muneeba Ali ends up lofting it towards mid on. Sophie Devine takes a sharp catch there.
Commentary.Howout: c Sophie Devine b Rosemary Mair

Commentary.Commentary: Full length, outside off. Muneeba Ali defends it out.
Length ball, wide outside off. Muneeba Ali slashes at it but misses.
Slower one, on a length, outside off. Ali does not go chasing away from her body.
WIDE! Short ball, down leg. Ali leaves it alone. Wide called by the umpire.
FOUR! What a shot! This is exquisite. Full length, wide outside off. Muneeba Ali frees her arms this time and carves it through cover-point for a boundary.
Full length, angled across the left-hander, wide outside off. Muneeba Ali has no shot to offer.
End of Powerplay 1! Now, 4 fielders can be placed outside the inner circle until the end of the 40th over.
Full, on off. Muneeba Ali gets forward and works it towards covers for a single.
Full and outside off, Muneeba Ali drills it to cover.
Slower through the air, outside off. Muneeba Ali shapes up for a sweep but is too early. The ball goes off the under edge past the keeper to third man for a couple.
Floats it up, on middle. Ali defends it out.
Full and on middle, Ali pushes it to mid off.
Bismah Maroof is the new batter in.

OUT! TAKEN! Frances Mackay gets the breakthrough. Loopy ball, outside off. Sidra Ameen goes  down on one knee to hoick but gets a top edge, the ball goes straight up as Brooke Halliday comes around and pouches a good catch.
Commentary.Howout: c Brooke Halliday b Frances Mackay

Commentary.Commentary: On a length, on middle. Sidra Ameen tucks it to mid-wicket. She calls for a single but then says no. Muneeba Ali had already started running and the fielder scores a direct hit at the bowler's end but Ali made it back in time. The batters take a single off overthrows.
Fuller, on off. Ameen prods and drives it back to the bowler.
Full and outside off, Sidra Ameen goes chasing and drives it but finds the cover fielder.
Back of a length, on off. Sidra Ameen hops and taps it to point.
Full and on off, played to mid on.
Good-length ball, on off. Sidra Ameen punches it towards covers.
Tossed up, on off. Ali taps it to point.
On middle, kept out.
Floats it up, on off. Ali defends it off the back foot.
Tossed up, outside off. Ali presses forward and defends it to cover.
Full and wide outside off, Sidra Ameen hits it uppishly over point for a single.
Loopy ball, on off. Sidra Ameen stays back and defends it back to the bowler.
Change. Frances Mackay comes into the attack now.
On off, blocked out. Another good over for Pakistan Women.
Now pushes this full bal through point for a brace. Good batting!

FOUR! Boundaries are coming along nicely for Pakistan Women! Length ball, on middle. Muneeba Ali gets low and smacks it to deep square leg for a boundary. No chance for the fine leg fielder to cut it off there.
Length, on the pads. Ali turns it to square leg.
Good length, outside off. Ali taps it to backward point.
Fullish, on off. Muneeba Ali blocks it solidly towards covers.
FOUR! An expensive over from Hannah Rowe! Short again on leg, Sidra Ameen pulls it along the carpet to fine leg for a boundary. 15 runs from the over.
On a length, on leg. Ali turns it to square leg for a run.
SIX! Mighty hit! Short ball, on middle and leg. Muneeba Ali waits for it, swivels and pulls it nicely over deep backward square leg for a biggie.
Length ball, outside off. Muneeba Ali drives it through covers for a couple of runs.
Full and on off, Sidra Ameen pushes it to mid on for a quick single.
Length ball, on middle. Sidra Ameen defends it out.
WIDE! Full and down leg, Sidra Ameen leaves it alone. Wided.
Full toss, on middle and leg. Muneeba Ali pulls it to mid-wicket.
WIDE! A loosener this time. Full, sliding down leg. Ali fails to pick it up. Wide called.
Five dots in a row! Yorker length delivery, on middle. Ali digs it out back to the bowler.
Full length, outside off. Ali taps it to point.
Length, on off. Ali defends it out.
Fuller, on off. Ali pushes it to mid off.
Good length, outside off. Ali leaves it alone for the keeper.
Length ball, on off. Ali clips it to mid-wicket for a single.
Full length, swinging in on off. Ali blocks it back to the bowler.
Length ball, on leg. Muneeba Ali defends it out.
Full length, on the pads. Sidra Ameen flicks it to mid-wicket for a single.
WIDE! Full length, angled down leg. Sidra Ameen looks to flick it away but misses. Wide called.
Full length, on middle and leg. Ameen blocks it out.
FOUR! Sidra Ameen gets her first boundary now. Back of a length, outside off. Sidra Ameen cuts it through point for a boundary.
A tidy over by Jess Kerr comes to an end. Just a single off it. The last delivery is bowled full and on the stumps. Ali bunts it out back to the bowler.
Full length, wide outside off. Sidra Ameen pushes it through point for a single.
Full inswinging delivery, outside off. Sidra Ameen taps it to the off side.
Short ball, on off. Ameen hangs back and defends it out solidly.
Full, outside off. Ameen slashes it to cover.
Length ball, on the stumps. Sidra Ameen defends it out watchfully.
FOUR! Nicely played! Muneeba Ali gets the first boundary of the chase. Fuller, wide outside off. Muneeba Ali reaches out and carves it through point for a boundary.
Full length, on the pads. Ali clips it to square leg.
Full length, just outside off. Ali leaves it alone for the keeper.
Another full delivery, angled across on off. Ali eases it to mid off.
Full length, around off, shaping away. Muneeba Ali pushes it to cover.
Back of a length, outside off. Ameen rides the bounce and cuts it to deep point for a single. She gets off the mark this time.
Full length, outside off. Muneeba Ali drives it to cover on the up.
On  a length, on off. Ali blocks it to cover.
Length ball, wide outside off. Ali waits for the ball, tries to guide it through the slip cordon but the fielder at first slip does well to make a half stop.
Fuller, angled across on off. Ali defends it on the front foot.
Back of a length, outside off. Muneeba Ali stays back and cuts it through covers for a brace.
Good length, angled across the left-hander. Muneeba Ali leaves it alone for the keeper.
